questions.text: Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Section 804, courts under what minimum horizontal dimension do not comply, and is the total court area or the least dimension the controlling dimension?

options.text: Courts under 2.00 m in least dimension do not comply; the least dimension is the controlling measure
Courts under 3.00 m in least dimension do not comply; the total area is the controlling measure
Courts under 1.50 m in least dimension do not comply; the total area is the controlling measure
Courts under 2.00 m in least dimension do not comply; the total area is the controlling measure

questions.rationale: The court least dimension minimum (2.00 m) equals the habitable room least dimension (2.00 m) and the temporary walkway minimum (1.20 m × ... actually no). These convergences across rules are intentional — the code uses consistent dimensional language across related provisions.

questions.text: A naturally ventilated master bedroom is 25.00 sq.m; its en-suite bathroom is 4.00 sq.m. Under PD 1096 Rule VIII, Section 808, what are the minimum required free areas of windows for each room?

options.text: Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.20 sq.m
Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.24 sq.m
Bedroom: 1.00 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.24 sq.m
Bedroom: 2.50 sq.m; Bathroom: 0.40 sq.m

questions.rationale: The bathroom window calculation tests two skills: (1) knowing the 5% rule for bathrooms (not the general 10%); (2) applying the absolute minimum floor (0.24 sq.m > 0.20 sq.m computed, so 0.24 sq.m governs). This is a classic 'more restrictive' rule.

questions.text: Per the 2004 Revised IRR, Rule XV, Section 1501, which of the following is an IRR-only addition not found in the original PD 1096 basic law?

options.text: Testing for structural adequacy and fire resistance, which ensures compliance with modern safety standards
Anchorage to withstand all probable external and internal forces, which is critical for structural integrity
A Safety Engineer must be present at the site during placement of prefabricated assemblies
Connections must develop member strength as an integral structure, which is essential for load distribution

questions.rationale: The Safety Engineer requirement during placement is exclusively an IRR addition. Options A, B, and D are all present in both the 1977 basic law and the 2004 IRR — they are the original provisions. The IRR also added: uPVC as named material, metal/uPVC-specific anchorage provision, inspection requirement, and Safety Engineer requirement.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 104, which of the following is a continuing obligation — not merely a one-time compliance event — under PD 1096?

options.text: Structural design calculations, which are typically a one-time requirement during the design phase
Maintenance of buildings in safe, sanitary, and good working condition
Submission of building permit applications, required only at the start of construction projects
Engagement of licensed professionals for plan preparation, necessary before construction begins

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 104, all buildings shall be maintained in safe, sanitary, and good working condition — indefinitely, not just at time of construction. This is a continuing code obligation that runs with the land, not just a one-time compliance event at the Certificate of Occupancy stage.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 106, an owner replaces all damaged ceramic floor tiles with new imported marble of higher quality. The work is classified as:

options.text: Repair, which involves restoring the original condition without upgrading materials
Renovation
Alteration, which includes changing the layout or function of a space
Addition, which involves expanding the existing structure by adding new elements

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, Renovation is any physical change made on a building to increase the value and/or improve the aesthetic quality of the building. Repair is remedial work to restore to original condition. Replacing ceramic with marble improves value and aesthetics — this is Renovation, not Repair (the result is an upgrade, not a restoration). The trigger being damage is irrelevant — what matters is the outcome.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 106, which government official is the Executive Officer of the OBO (Office of the Building Official)?

options.text: The Mayor of the city or municipality, who oversees all local government operations including building regulations
The Building Official, appointed by the DPWH Secretary
The Executive Director of the NBCDO, responsible for national building code development and enforcement
The Secretary of DPWH, who has overarching authority over public works and highways

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, the Building Official is the Executive Officer of the OBO, appointed by the DPWH Secretary. The OBO is the office authorized to enforce the Code and IRR. The Building Official has authority to issue permits, certificates of occupancy, stop-work orders, and demolition orders.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 106, what is the key characteristic that distinguishes CONVERSION from other change-type definitions?

options.text: It involves physical changes to the building structure, such as alterations to load-bearing elements
It involves a change in the use or occupancy of the building that has different requirements
It always involves an increase in floor area, typically requiring additional structural support
It requires the demolition of existing structural elements, which may affect the building's integrity

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, Conversion is any change in the use or occupancy of buildings or parts thereof that has different requirements. Unlike Repair, Renovation, Alteration, and Addition — which focus on physical changes — Conversion is about USE. A building can be converted without any construction at all (reclassifying occupancy), though physical work often accompanies it.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 103, what is the relationship between referral codes and PD 1096?

options.text: Referral codes replace PD 1096 when there is a conflict, ensuring that the most current standards are applied
Referral codes are supplementary to PD 1096 and apply when PD 1096 does not directly address a technical matter
Referral codes take precedence over PD 1096 in all cases, providing a more comprehensive regulatory framework
Referral codes apply only to private buildings, not public buildings, which are governed by separate regulations

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 103, applicable provisions of codes and standards of various professional organizations, government agencies, and technical associations are deemed Referral Codes — supplementary to PD 1096. They apply when PD 1096 does not directly address a technical matter. Examples: NSCP (structural), PEC (electrical), PSME Code (mechanical), PCAB standards.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 106, what is the key distinguishing feature that separates an ADDITION from an ALTERATION under the National Building Code?

options.text: Alterations involve structural changes while additions do not, focusing instead on expanding existing spaces
Additions increase height and/or floor area; alterations do not increase height and/or floor area
Additions require a licensed engineer while alterations do not, as they are considered less complex
Alterations are more extensive than additions, often requiring comprehensive redesign and approval

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, an Addition is new construction that increases height and/or floor area of an existing building. An Alteration is any change in materials, partitioning, openings, structural parts, or utilities that does NOT increase height and/or floor area. The 'and/or' means increasing EITHER height OR floor area constitutes an Addition.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 104, the word 'shall' appears in all requirements. Under Philippine statutory construction, what does 'shall' mean?

options.text: Discretionary — the official may choose to apply the requirement
Mandatory — the requirement must be complied with
Advisory — compliance is recommended but not required
Conditional — compliance is required only if the Building Official demands it

questions.rationale: Under Philippine statutory construction, 'shall' is mandatory. All three requirements of Sec. 104 — conformity to safe construction principles, suitability to purpose, and maintenance in safe/sanitary condition — use 'shall.' A building official cannot approve non-compliant plans, and a building owner has a continuing mandatory obligation to maintain the building.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Section 103 and IRR Sec. 103, which of the following is explicitly exempt from the coverage of the National Building Code?

options.text: A socialized housing project developed under BP 220
A three-storey residential condominium in a mixed-use development
A factory building owned by a government-owned corporation
A single-family residence using modern construction materials

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 103, buildings covered by BP 220 (Economic and Socialized Housing) are explicitly exempt from PD 1096 and governed instead by HLURB/DHSUD standards. Note: this exception appears in the 2004 IRR but NOT in the original PD 1096 Sec. 103. Traditional indigenous family dwellings are also exempt under Sec. 103 of the basic law.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 103, how many disciplines does PD 1096 explicitly cover?

options.text: 5 disciplines
6 disciplines
7 disciplines
8 disciplines

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 103, the Code covers 7 disciplines: Architectural, Civil/Structural, Electrical, Mechanical, Sanitary, Plumbing, and Electronics. Each discipline requires a licensed professional to sign and seal relevant plans and documents.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 105, every site intended for human habitation must maintain safe distance from which three categories of hazards?

options.text: Noise sources, fire hazards, and radiation sources, which are critical for ensuring a safe living environment
Streams/bodies of water/air pollution sources, volcanic sites, and buildings posing fire or explosion risk
High-voltage power lines, flood-prone areas, and fault lines, which are essential considerations for site safety
Landslide-prone areas, coastal erosion zones, and earthquake epicenters, which are vital for risk mitigation

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 105, sites for human habitation must be sanitary, hygienic, and safe. Safe distance must be maintained from: (1) streams, bodies of water, and sources of air pollution; (2) volcanic sites or active/potentially active volcanoes; (3) buildings that constitute a potential source of fire or explosion. Mnemonic: 'SASH' — Streams/Air pollution, Active volcanic sites, Safe distance required, Habitation triggers.

questions.text: Per PD 1096, Section 102 (Declaration of Policy), what type of standards does the National Building Code establish?

options.text: Optimal standards and requirements for building construction, ensuring safety and efficiency
Maximum standards that may not be exceeded in any building, to prevent overbuilding and ensure compliance
Minimum standards and requirements for building construction and use
Recommended guidelines for architects and engineers, providing a framework for best practices

questions.rationale: Per PD 1096, Sec. 102, the Code provides a framework of minimum standards and requirements. The operative word is 'minimum.' The Code does not prescribe optimal or maximum standards. Local governments, project specifications, and referral codes may exceed minimums; nothing in PD 1096 prevents that. What they cannot do is fall below.

questions.text: Per IRR Sec. 103, existing buildings constructed without building permits may be legalized under what conditions?

options.text: Payment of a nominal registration fee only, with no structural upgrades required
Conformity to all current code requirements plus payment of penalties, surcharges, and fines
Structural upgrades only, without requiring compliance with other code provisions
Full demolition and reconstruction to current code standards at the owner's expense

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 103, existing buildings constructed without permits may be legalized if they are made to conform to all current code requirements, subject to corresponding penalties, surcharges, and fines. This is not a blanket amnesty — it requires full code compliance (not just the code at original construction) plus all financial penalties. This IRR provision does not appear in the original PD 1096 basic law.

questions.text: A contractor encloses an existing open terrace to create a new room — adding gross floor area without adding height. Under IRR Sec. 106, this work is correctly classified as:

options.text: Alteration — changes to materials and partitioning within the existing building footprint
Renovation — physical change that increases the use and aesthetic quality of the building
Addition — new construction that increases the floor area of the existing building
Conversion — change in the use of the previously open terrace to an enclosed room

questions.rationale: Per IRR Sec. 106, an Addition is new construction that increases height and/or floor area. The 'and/or' means increasing EITHER height OR floor area alone constitutes an Addition. Enclosing a terrace increases gross floor area without adding height; therefore the work is classified as an Addition, requiring an addition building permit. This is a common exam trap where candidates assume both dimensions must change.
